saints.name: St. Catherine of Sweden
saints.title: Virgin, Abbess of Vadstena
saints.shortBlurb: The daughter of St. Bridget of Sweden who followed her mother to Rome and led the new Bridgettine order at Vadstena…
biography: Born about 1331, the fourth child of St. Bridget of Sweden and Ulf Gudmarsson, Catherine was married at about twelve or thirteen to Lord Eggert van Kyren, a German nobleman, whom she persuaded to join her in a vow of perpetual chastity. In 1349 she accompanied her mother to Rome, and soon after their arrival her husband died.

For some twenty-five years she shared her mother's pilgrimages and works of charity, journeying with her as far as the Holy Land. When Bridget died in 1373, Catherine brought her body home to Sweden for burial at Vadstena and became the first abbess of the monastery her mother had founded there.

Returning to Rome, she labored for her mother's canonization and for the confirmation of the Bridgettine order, living five years in friendship with St. Catherine of Siena. She died at Vadstena on 24 March 1381; her cult was confirmed by Innocent VIII in 1484.
saints.knownFor: Leading the Bridgettine order at Vadstena.

canonization.canonized: Cult confirmed 1484 by Pope Innocent VIII

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 24 March
